how.d: Short, plain-English explanations — no grammar walls, no jargon without a translation.
Each phrase speaks in a native Tamil voice. Slow it to 0.2× and repeat until it sticks.
Every topic ends in practice: quiz yourself, then review the words until they stay.

hfaqs.a: No. Start with spoken Tamil in Roman letters, and let the script come second. Learners who speak first stay motivated far longer than learners who drill letters for a month before saying a word.
hfaqs.q: Must I learn the Tamil script before speaking?

hfaqs.a: வணக்கம் for respect, ஆம் and இல்லை, நன்றி, தயவுசெய்து, சரி, and நான் — I. With those seven you can open any interaction in Tamil Nadu politely while your vocabulary grows underneath.
hfaqs.q: Which words should I learn in week one?

hfaqs.a: The Dravidian sounds new to most ears — ழ் (zh), the rolled ர, the three n's and l's. Ten minutes of daily listening retunes your ears within weeks; the pronunciation page walks you through each one.
hfaqs.q: What is the hardest part of Tamil?

topics.desc: வணக்கம் opens every door in Tamil Nadu — plus mornings, welcomes and warm goodbyes. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes, and nobody will mind — வணக்கம் with folded hands is understood and loved everywhere Tamil is spoken. With close friends a smile and நலமா? (nalamaa — are you well?) feels warmer.
faqs.q: Can I just say vanakkam everywhere?

faqs.a: வணக்கம் with folded hands and a small nod, and நீங்கள் (neenga — formal you) until invited closer. Add அண்ணா (annaa) or அக்கா (akkaa) for someone slightly older — it warms everything instantly.
faqs.q: How do I greet an elder respectfully?

faqs.a: பிறகு பார்க்கலாம் (piragu paarkkalaam — we'll meet again later) is the warm standard. சென்று வாருங்கள் (sendru vaarungal — go and come back) is the classic elder's farewell — receive it with a smile and a nod.
faqs.q: How do Tamils say goodbye?

topics.note: A note on நலமா vs சௌக்கியமா. நலமா? (nalamaa) is the everyday are you well? — warm, quick, everywhere. சௌக்கியமா? (saukkiyamaa) is its formal elder cousin, heard at weddings and festivals. Start with நலமா; graduate to சௌக்கியமா when aunties adopt you.
paras: வணக்கம் (vanakkam) is the one greeting that never fails. Folded hands, a small nod, and it works with strangers, elders, shopkeepers and officials — exactly the people a learner meets first. Say it clearly, hold the folded hands half a second, and Tamil Nadu opens to you.

Mornings get their own greeting: காலை வணக்கம் (kaalai vanakkam — good morning), heard in offices, schools and tea stalls until about eleven. Evenings soften to மாலை வணக்கம் (maalai vanakkam). Time-stamped greetings signal that you live in the language, not just visit it.

Welcomes are grand in Tamil culture: வாருங்கள் (vaarungal — please come/welcome) opens homes, shops and hearts. Guests are greeted standing, often with water or coffee before a single question. Return the warmth — வந்துவிட்டேன், நன்றி (I've come, thank you) — and you are family within minutes.

Goodbyes promise return, never end: பிறகு பார்க்கலாம் (we'll meet again later) is the everyday farewell; பார்த்துக்கொள்ளுங்கள் (take care) adds affection. Leave every conversation with a வணக்கம் and a smile — in Tamil Nadu, how you leave is remembered longer than how you came.
topics.title: Saying hello the Tamil way

topics.desc: 12 vowels, 18 consonants and the famous ழ் — the Tamil alphabet without tears. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Twelve vowels (உயிர்), eighteen consonants (மெய்), one aytham (ஃ) — 31 letters that combine into 247 total shapes. Sounds huge, behaves simply: learn the 12 + 18 and the combinations assemble themselves.
faqs.q: How many letters does Tamil have?

faqs.a: ழ் (zh) — a sound between r, l and d made with the tongue curled back. தமிழ் itself contains it, so every Tamil learner must conquer it. Listen, curl, practise: it arrives within weeks.
faqs.q: What is the hardest Tamil letter?

faqs.a: No — Tamil has no aspirated consonants (no kh, gh, th, bh). One க covers ka, kha, ga and gha by position. Fewer letters to learn, smarter rules to love.
faqs.q: Does Tamil have kh, gh, bh sounds?

topics.note: A note on the pulli (்). The tiny dot above a consonant kills its hidden vowel: க is ka, க் is just k. Tamil writes pure consonants with the pulli and syllables without — க் + அ = க. One dot, and the whole reading system clicks.
paras: Tamil vowels (உயிர் எழுத்து — life letters) come in twelve: அ ஆ இ ஈ உ ஊ எ ஏ ஐ ஒ ஓ ஔ, plus the special ஃ (aytham). Short and long pairs — அ/ஆ, இ/ஈ, உ/ஊ — change meaning completely: கல் (kal — stone) versus கால் (kaal — leg). Length is meaning in Tamil; stretch with care.

Consonants (மெய் எழுத்து — body letters) number eighteen: க் ங் ச் ஞ் ட் ண் த் ந் ப் ம் ய் ர் ல் வ் ழ் ள் ற் ன். Notice what's missing: no aspirates, no separate voiced letters. One letter per mouth position, pronounced soft or hard by rule — Tamil spelling is famously faithful to speech.

Vowels and consonants marry into உயிர்மெய் (uyirmei) combinations: க் + அ = க (ka), க் + ஆ = கா (kaa). Twelve vowels times eighteen consonants gives 216 combos plus the 31 originals — 247 shapes from simple, predictable joins. Learn the joins, not the list.

Then the crown jewel: ழ் (zh), the retroflex approximant Tamil is famous for — தமிழ், வாழ்க்கை, பழம். Curl the tongue back without touching the roof, voice it, and feel the most Tamil sound in existence. Natives will grin when you land it; the grin is worth weeks of practice.
topics.title: Tamil alphabet

topics.desc: ஒன்று இரண்டு மூன்று to நூறு — plus clock time and the ancient Tamil digits. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Both, mixed freely — but learn international digits for daily life (prices, phones, buses all use them) and recognise Tamil digits (௦௧௨௩...) for temples, invitations and proverbs. The ancient digits survive in ceremony, not commerce.
faqs.q: Tamil digits or international digits?

faqs.a: Take the number, add மணி (mani — bell/hour): மூன்று மணி (three o'clock). Half past adds அரை (arai) — மூன்றரை மணி is half past three. One rule, every clock in Tamil Nadu.
faqs.q: How do I say the time in Tamil?

faqs.a: எவ்வளவு? (evvalavu — how much?). Then listen for the number plus ரூபாய் (roobaai — rupees). Market Tamil is the fastest teacher there is.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

topics.lede: ஒன்று இரண்டு மூன்று — numbers, clock time and market-ready counting.

links.desc: Numbers in course order, with drills.
links.label: Tamil numbers

topics.note: A note on ௦௧௨௩௪௫௬௭௮௯. Tamil has its own ancient digits — ௧ ௨ ௩ ௪ ௫ ௬ ௭ ௮ ௯ ௰ ௱ ௲ — beautiful and nearly retired. You'll meet them on temple walls and wedding invitations. Learn to recognise them for joy; use international digits for life.
paras: One to ten: ஒன்று (ondru), இரண்டு (irandu), மூன்று (moondru), நான்கு (naangu), ஐந்து (aindu), ஆறு (aaru), ஏழு (eezhu), எட்டு (ettu), ஒன்பது (onbadu), பத்து (patthu). Chant them in rhythm — Tamil numbers love rhythm — and they stick in days, not weeks.

Eleven to nineteen build on பத்து: பதினொன்று (11), பன்னிரண்டு (12), பதிமூன்று (13)... then the tens march: இருபது (20), முப்பது (30), நாற்பது (40), ஐம்பது (50), அறுபது (60), எழுபது (70), எண்பது (80), தொண்ணூறு (90), நூறு (100). Past twenty, glue tens to units — இருபத்து ஒன்று (21) — and count to a thousand (ஆயிரம்) without fear.

Money runs on numbers: the currency is the ரூபாய் (roobaai — rupee), and எவ்வளவு? (evvalavu — how much?) is the most useful sentence in Tamil Nadu. Listen for the number, repeat it back — ஐம்பது? (fifty?) — and your first Tamil transaction completes itself.

Time reuses numbers with மணி (mani — hour): இரண்டு மணி (two o'clock), ஐந்து மணி (five o'clock). இப்போது மணி என்ன? (ippodu mani enna — what time is it now?) is the question; half hours add அரை (arai — half). Numbers, money, clocks: one skill, three daily victories.
topics.title: Counting in Tamil

topics.desc: Names, homes and small talk — your first real Tamil conversations, line by line. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: உங்கள் பெயர் என்ன? (ungal peyar enna — what is your name?) for respect; உன் பெயர் என்ன? (un peyar enna) for friends and children. Answer with என் பெயர்... (en peyar — my name is...). Names first, always.
faqs.q: How do I ask someone's name?

faqs.a: நீங்கள் எங்கிருந்து வருகிறீர்கள்? (where are you from?) — then answer for yourself: நான் ... இருந்து வருகிறேன். Origin questions are the universal second question; prepare your answer before you need it.
faqs.q: How do I say where I'm from?

faqs.a: மெதுவாகப் பேசுங்கள் (please speak slowly) and மீண்டும் சொல்லுங்கள் (please say it again). Said with a smile, these two sentences make every Tamil speaker slow down and help.
faqs.q: What do I say when people speak too fast?

topics.note: A note on நீங்கள், நீ and the missing middle. Tamil has two yous where English has one: நீங்கள் (neenga — formal/plural) and நீ (nee — familiar). No three-level ladder like Bengali — just respect versus closeness. Start with நீங்கள் for every adult; let friendship invite you to நீ.
paras: Every first conversation follows the same dance: வணக்கம், உங்கள் பெயர் என்ன? (what is your name?), என் பெயர்... (my name is...), நீங்கள் எங்கிருந்து வருகிறீர்கள்? (where are you from?). Four lines, and you have had a real conversation. Practise them in order until they flow without thinking.

Small talk runs on three questions: நீங்கள் என்ன செய்கிறீர்கள்? (what do you do?), தமிழ் பேசுவீர்களா? (do you speak Tamil?), சாப்பிட்டீர்களா? (have you eaten? — asked with genuine care). Answer briefly, ask back immediately — உங்களுக்கு? நீங்கள்? — because conversations are volleys, not speeches.

When the torrent comes — and Tamil hospitality pours words — deploy the brakes: மெதுவாகப் பேசுங்கள் (please speak slowly), எனக்குப் புரியவில்லை (I don't understand), மீண்டும் சொல்லுங்கள் (please say it again). Every Tamil speaker honours these instantly; they are the learner's seatbelt.

Close warmly and promise return: உங்களைச் சந்தித்ததில் மகிழ்ச்சி (pleased to meet you), மீண்டும் சந்திப்போம் (we'll meet again), பிறகு பார்க்கலாம் (see you later). Leave with a வணக்கம் and the door stays open — Tamil conversations end the way they begin: with folded hands.
topics.title: Real Tamil conversation

topics.desc: போ, வா, சாப்பிடு — the twelve verbs that run daily life, plus how they bend. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Stems are orders to friends — போ! (go!), வா! (come!), சாப்பிடு! (eat!). Polite speech adds endings: போங்கள் (please go), வாருங்கள் (please come). Learn stems first, politeness second, and never order a stranger.
faqs.q: Are verb stems commands?

faqs.a: நான் போகிறேன் (I go), நீ போகிறாய் (you go), அவர் போகிறார் (he/she formal goes). Person-markers on every verb — நான்/நீ/அவர் each pull their own ending. Drill one verb through all persons and the pattern owns you.
faqs.q: How do Tamil verbs change?

faqs.a: இல்லை (illai — no/not) negates nouns and adjectives — எனக்குத் தெரியாது uses -ஆது for verbs (I don't know). Tamil negation splits by word type; learn இல்லை for things, வேண்டாம் (vendaam — don't want) for refusals.
faqs.q: How do I say no to a verb?

topics.note: A note on வாருங்கள் vs வா. வா (vaa) orders a friend to come; வாருங்கள் (vaarungal) welcomes a guest like royalty. Same verb, different universe — the -ங்கள் ending is pure respect. When in doubt, add the respect: Tamils forgive stiff politeness instantly and casual rudeness never.
paras: Twelve verbs carry daily life: போ (go), வா (come), சாப்பிடு (eat), குடி (drink), படி (read/study), எழுது (write), செய் (do), பேசு (speak), கொடு (give), எடு (take), இரு (be/stay), பார் (see). Memorise these stems and you can order food, find toilets, make friends and survive beautifully.

Stems bend by person in the present: நான் போகிறேன் (I go), நீ போகிறாய் (you familiar go), நீங்கள் போகிறீர்கள் (you formal go), அவர் போகிறார் (he/she formal goes). The -கிற- (kira) infix marks present tense across nearly every verb — one infix, hundreds of verbs, instant sentences.

Polite commands add -ங்கள்: போங்கள் (please go), வாருங்கள் (please come), சாப்பிடுங்கள் (please eat), சொல்லுங்கள் (please say). This one ending turns every order into an invitation — it is the most useful suffix in Tamil, worth more than a hundred nouns.

Negation and existence close the kit: இருக்கிறது (irukkiradhu — it is / there is) anchors locations — புத்தகம் மேசையில் இருக்கிறது (the book is on the table). இல்லை (illai — there isn't) removes — பணம் இல்லை (no money). Twelve verbs plus இருக்கிறது/இல்லை: the engine room of Tamil.
topics.title: Tamil verbs

topics.desc: Water, money, time, today — the everyday Tamil words that unlock daily life. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Time words first: இன்று (today), நாளை (tomorrow), நேற்று (yesterday), இப்போது (now). You will use them ten times a day — shopping, planning, chatting — while rare nouns gather dust.
faqs.q: Which words pay off fastest?

faqs.a: Tamil happily absorbs English — பஸ் (bus), டிக்கெட் (ticket), ஆபீஸ் (office). Use the pure Tamil word when you know it (பேருந்து, நுழைவுச்சீட்டு), the loanword when you don't. Fluency first, purity later.
faqs.q: Is mixing English okay?

faqs.a: Nouns first, verbs second, adjectives third. With fifty nouns and the twelve verbs from the verbs page, you can point, ask and survive — grammar glues them later.
faqs.q: Nouns or verbs first?

topics.note: A note on இன்று, நாளை, நேற்று. Tamil time words pivot around today: இன்று (indru — today), நாளை (naalai — tomorrow), நேற்று (nettru — yesterday). Master this trio and half your daily sentences assemble themselves — நாளை பார்க்கலாம் (see you tomorrow) alone is worth the lesson.
paras: Survival runs on nouns: தண்ணீர் (thanneer — water), உணவு (unavu — food), வீடு (veedu — home), பணம் (panam — money), நேரம் (neram — time). Five words, and you can ask for water, find home, handle money and ask the time — the entire first day in a new city.

Movement words come next: சாலை (saalai — road), பேருந்து (perundu — bus), கடை (kadai — shop), பள்ளி (palli — school). Tamil cities move by bus and foot; knowing பேருந்து நிலையம் எங்கே? (where is the bus stand?) saves more time than any app.

Opinions need adjectives: நல்ல (nalla — good), பெரிய (periya — big), சிறிய (siriya — small), புதிய (pudiya — new), பழைய (pazhaya — old). நல்லது (nalladhu — that's good) approves everything from food to plans — the most useful single opinion in Tamil.

Weather and mood close the kit: மழை (mazhai — rain) matters half the year, வெயில் (veyil — sun/heat) the other half. மழை வருகிறது (rain is coming) starts conversations with strangers; in Tamil Nadu, weather talk is friendship's front door.
topics.title: Core Tamil vocabulary

topics.desc: Idli, dosai, filter kaapi — order like a local, from breakfast to bill. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Point and say இது ஒன்று (idhu ondru — one of these) — it works in every mess, canteen and bakery in Tamil Nadu. Add தயவுசெய்து (please) and a smile; grammar can wait until dessert.
faqs.q: How do I order with almost no Tamil?

faqs.a: காரம் குறைவாக (kaaram kuraivaaga — less spicy, please). Tamil food honours chilli deeply; this one sentence saves sensitive stomachs while keeping every flavour.
faqs.q: How do I ask for less spicy food?

faqs.a: ருசியாக இருக்கிறது (rusiyaaga irukkiradhu — it's delicious). Say it to the cook, the server, the auntie who packed your lunch — it is the highest compliment in Tamil food culture.
faqs.q: How do I praise the food?

topics.note: A note on காபி. Filter kaapi — strong decoction, frothed milk, drunk from the dabara-tumbler — is not coffee, it is a morning ritual. Order ஒரு காபி (oru kaapi — one coffee) at any stall, watch it cool mid-air between vessels, and understand Tamil Nadu in one sip.
paras: Breakfast is the glory: இட்லி (idli — steamed rice cakes), தோசை (dosai — crisp crepe), பொங்கல் (pongal — rice-lentil comfort), வடை (vadai — savoury doughnut), all served with சாம்பார் (saambaar) and சட்னி (chutney). டிபன் சாப்பிட்டீர்களா? (have you had tiffin?) is asked with love — answer honestly, then accept seconds.

Meals centre on சாப்பாடு (saappaadu — the rice meal): rice, சாம்பார், ரசம் (rasam — pepper-tamarind soup), கூட்டு (koottu — lentil-vegetable), தயிர் (tayir — curd), அப்பளம் (appalam — crisp papad). Served on banana leaves at weddings, eaten with the right hand — சாப்பாடு ரெடியா? (is the meal ready?) is the happiest question.

Taste words steer every order: காரம் (kaaram — spicy), இனிப்பு (inippu — sweet), புளிப்பு (pulippu — sour), உப்பு (uppu — salt). கொஞ்சம் உப்பு (a little salt), சர்க்கரை வேண்டாம் (no sugar) — with taste words, your plate obeys you.

Drinks and bills close the meal: காபி (filter coffee), தேநீர் (theneer — tea), மோர் (moor — buttermilk), பழச்சாறு (pazhachcharu — juice). கணக்கு கொடுங்கள் (kanakku kodungal — please give the bill) ends it; ருசியாக இருந்தது (it was delicious) guarantees a smile on your way out.
topics.title: Food phrases

topics.desc: ழ், three n's, two r's — every tricky Tamil sound, one by one, with examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes — ந் (alveolar, like English n), ன் (dental, tongue on teeth), ண் (retroflex, tongue curled back). மன் (man — mind/mud) versus மண் (mann — soil) is a real minimal pair; natives hear the difference instantly.
faqs.q: Does Tamil really have three n sounds?

faqs.a: ர is a light flap (like the dd in American cuter); ற is a hard trill (rolled r). மரம் (maram — tree) versus மறம்? — flap soft, trill strong. Practise மரம் daily; the flap arrives first.
faqs.q: What is the difference between ர and ற?

faqs.a: Dental consonants touch the teeth (த், ந்), retroflexes curl the tongue back (ட், ண்). தரம் (tharam — quality) versus டமாரம்? — teeth versus roof. Exaggerate at first; subtlety follows.
faqs.q: Dental versus retroflex — help?

topics.lede: ழ், three n's, two r's — every tricky sound, one by one, with examples.

links.desc: Sounds in course order, with drills.
links.label: Tamil pronunciation

links.desc: Speak these sounds until they are yours.
links.label: Tamil practice lab

topics.note: A note on ழ் (zh). Tamil's signature sound: curl the tongue back toward the roof WITHOUT touching, and voice it — between r, l and a French j. தமிழ், பழம், வாழ்க்கை. Children take years to perfect it, so forgive yourself months — then enjoy the applause.
paras: The three n's sort by tongue position: ந் (alveolar — English-like n, as in நல்ல), ன் (dental — tongue on teeth, as in மீன்), ண் (retroflex — curled back, as in கண்). Say na-na-na sliding the tongue from ridge to teeth to roof — three letters, one glide.

The two r's split soft and hard: ர் is a single flap — மரம் (maram — tree), பெரிய (periya — big) — while ற் trills hard — பறவை (paravai — bird), வெற்றி (verri — victory). English ears merge them; Tamil meaning doesn't. Practise pairs daily until your tongue files them separately.

Dental versus retroflex stops: த் (teeth — தமிழ், தண்ணீர்) against ட் (roof — படம், வீடு). Hold a finger to your lips: dentals puff forward, retroflexes pop upward. Ten minutes of த-ட alternation retunes the mouth within a week.

The rest behave kindly: ச is cha at word start (சாப்பாடு) softening to sa inside words (பேசு), க hardens and softens by position (கடை, மகன்), and long vowels simply hold double — ஆ, ஈ, ஊ. Tamil spelling mirrors speech faithfully: pronounce what you see, and you are right nine times in ten.
topics.title: Tamil pronunciation

topics.desc: Verb last, respect built in — Tamil grammar in plain English, no jargon walls. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Put the verb last: நான் புத்தகம் படிக்கிறேன் (I book read). Subject-Object-Verb, always. English instincts will fight you for a week; then SOV feels like home.
faqs.q: Where does the verb go?

faqs.a: எனக்கு (enakku — to me), உனக்கு (unakku — to you familiar), உங்களுக்கு (ungalukku — to you formal). எனக்கு தண்ணீர் வேண்டும் (I want water) is literally to-me water is-wanted — Tamil wants flow toward people.
faqs.q: How do I say I want something?

faqs.a: இது (idhu — this, near me), அது (adhu — that, far). இது என்ன? (what is this?) points at anything within reach; mastery takes one shopping trip.
faqs.q: How do this and that work?

topics.lede: Verb last, respect built in — Tamil grammar in plain English.

links.desc: Grammar in course order, fully worked.
links.label: Tamil grammar

links.desc: Use this grammar in real exchanges.
links.label: Tamil conversation lessons

topics.note: A note on -க்கு (kku). Tamil's dative ending aims verbs at people and places: எனக்கு (to me), பள்ளிக்கு (to school), வீட்டுக்கு (homeward). Sentences like எனக்குப் புரிகிறது (to-me it-is-understood = I understand) reveal Tamil's worldview: experiences come TO you.
paras: Tamil sentences end with the verb: நான் புத்தகம் படிக்கிறேன் (I — book — read). Subject first, object middle, verb last — SOV, the order of half the world's languages. Rearrange your English instincts once, and every Tamil sentence parses cleanly.

Small endings do heavy work: -இல் (il — in/on) places things — வீட்டில் (at home), மேசையில் (on the table); -உடன் (udan — with) joins company — நண்பருடன் (with a friend); -க்கு (kku) aims motion and wanting — பள்ளிக்கு (to school), எனக்கு வேண்டும் (I want). Endings, not word order, carry Tamil meaning.

Questions rise at the end: நீங்கள் எங்கே போகிறீர்கள்? (where are you going?) — எங்கே (where), என்ன (what), யார் (who), ஏன் (why), எப்படி (how), எப்போது (when). Yes-no questions add -ஆ (-aa): சாப்பிட்டீர்களா? (have you eaten?). Question words plus rising tone — asking is easy.

Negation splits three ways: இல்லை (illai) denies existence — பணம் இல்லை (no money); verb endings deny actions — எனக்குத் தெரியாது (I don't know); வேண்டாம் (vendaam) refuses — சர்க்கரை வேண்டாம் (no sugar, thanks). Three no's for three jobs — Tamil refuses precisely.

phrases.en: I read a book (I book read)

topics.title: Tamil grammar

topics.desc: Your first Tamil week: yes, no, I, you, and ten sentences that survive anything. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: வணக்கம், ஆம், சரி, நன்றி, தயவுசெய்து — five words, infinite mileage. Add நான் and நீங்கள் and you can introduce yourself to anyone in Tamil Nadu.
faqs.q: What are the first five words?

faqs.a: Fifteen focused minutes beat two distracted hours. One topic page, every speaker tapped, five words reviewed — daily beats heroic.
faqs.q: How much should I study daily?

faqs.a: No — speak first, script second. Roman letters carry you through months of conversation; the alphabet page waits patiently until curiosity pulls you in.
faqs.q: Must I learn the script first?

topics.lede: Your first Tamil week: yes, no, I, you, and sentences that survive anything.

links.desc: The course start, step by step.
links.label: Tamil beginner course

topics.note: A note on ஆம், சரி and ஓ. Tamil yes comes in three flavours: ஆம் (aam — respectful yes), சரி (sari — okay/agreed), ஓ (oh — casual yeah). Learners live on ஆம் and சரி — respectful, warm, never wrong. Save ஓ for friends.
paras: Week one needs eleven words: வணக்கம் (hello), ஆம் (yes), சரி (okay), நன்றி (thanks), தயவுசெய்து (please), நான் (I), நீங்கள் (you, formal), இது என்ன? (what is this?), புரிகிறது (I understand), தெரியாது (I don't know), போகலாம் (let's go). Eleven words, and you can greet, agree, thank, ask, confess ignorance and move — the whole beginner game.

Pronouns branch early: நான் (I), நீங்கள் (you formal/plural), நீ (you familiar), அவர் (he/she formal), அவன்/அவள் (he/she familiar), நாங்கள் (we exclusive), நாம் (we inclusive). Two we's where English has one — நாம் போகலாம் (let's go, you included) is Tamil's warmest invitation.

Quantity words multiply everything: கொஞ்சம் (a little), நிறைய (a lot), போதும் (enough), மட்டும் (only). கொஞ்சம் தமிழ் பேசுகிறேன் (I speak a little Tamil) is the perfect learner's confession — humble, charming, instantly rewarded with help.

Action invitations close week one: இங்கே வாருங்கள் (come here), உட்காருங்கள் (please sit), சாப்பிடுங்கள் (please eat), போகலாம் (let's go). These four run hospitality, the beating heart of Tamil culture — learn them and you stop being a guest and start being family.
topics.title: Tamil for absolute beginners

topics.desc: அம்மா, அப்பா, அண்ணன், அக்கா — family words, including the elder-younger split. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes — Tamil splits siblings by age: அண்ணன் (elder brother) versus தம்பி (younger brother), அக்கா (elder sister) versus தங்கை (younger sister). Age order is grammar in Tamil families.
faqs.q: Why two words for brother?

faqs.a: அண்ணா (annaa) and அக்கா (akkaa) address any slightly-older man or woman — shopkeepers, colleagues, strangers. It borrows family warmth for the whole world.
faqs.q: Can I call strangers annaa and akkaa?

faqs.a: உங்கள் குடும்பத்தில் எத்தனை பேர்? (how many people in your family?) — then listen proudly to the answer. Family questions are love in Tamil culture.
faqs.q: How do I ask about family?

topics.lede: அம்மா, அப்பா, அண்ணன், அக்கா — family, including the elder-younger split.
topics.note: A note on அத்தை, மாமா and the cousin map. Tamil kinship is famously precise: அத்தை (father's sister / mother's brother's wife), மாமா (mother's brother / father's sister's husband), அண்ணி (elder brother's wife), each relation owns its word. Learners need the big six first; the full map unfolds at weddings.
paras: Parents anchor everything: அம்மா (ammaa — mother) and அப்பா (appaa — father) — the first words of every Tamil child and the warmest words in the language. அம்மா calls across market crowds; அப்பா advises over evening coffee. Learn them with love, not just memory.

Siblings split by age, never blend: அண்ணன் (elder brother), தம்பி (younger brother), அக்கா (elder sister), தங்கை (younger sister). There is no plain brother — every brother is elder or younger, and the word you choose declares the hierarchy. Ask ages early; address correctly always.

Grandparents rule the roost: தாத்தா (thaaththaa — grandfather) and பாட்டி (paatti — grandmother) — storytellers, sweet-sneakers, family courts of final appeal. பாட்டி கதை (grandmother's tale) is a whole genre; தாத்தா advice ends arguments. Respect flows upward; treats flow down.

The wider net holds daily life: மாமா (uncle), அத்தை (auntie), கணவர் (husband), மனைவி (wife), குடும்பம் (family itself). என் குடும்பம் (my family) introduces them all — practise the sentence with your own names filled in, because you will say it at every Tamil gathering forever.
topics.title: Family words

topics.desc: Seven days, four day-parts, weeks and months — Tamil time from morning to month. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Start the week Sunday like Tamil calendars: ஞாயிறு, திங்கள், செவ்வாய், புதன், வியாழன், வெள்ளி, சனி. Chant them in order — rhythm makes them permanent.
faqs.q: How do I memorise the days?

faqs.a: காலை (morning), மதியம் (afternoon), மாலை (evening), இரவு (night). Greetings, meals and plans all key off these four — மாலை வணக்கம் (good evening) after four-ish.
faqs.q: How does Tamil split the day?

faqs.a: வாரம் (vaaram — week), மாதம் (maadham — month), வருடம் (varudam — year). அடுத்த வாரம் (next week), இந்த மாதம் (this month) — plans assemble instantly.
faqs.q: Week, month, year?

topics.lede: Seven days, four day-parts, weeks and months — Tamil time fully told.

links.desc: Clocks and calendars in course order.
links.label: Tamil time and dates

topics.note: A note on வெள்ளி and செவ்வாய். Friday (வெள்ளி) and Tuesday (செவ்வாய்) are auspicious days — temples fill, new ventures launch, அம்மன் worship peaks. Knowing the days means knowing the rhythm: never schedule a sceptical meeting on a festival Friday.
paras: The week runs Sunday-first: ஞாயிறு (Sunday), திங்கள் (Monday), செவ்வாய் (Tuesday), புதன் (Wednesday), வியாழன் (Thursday), வெள்ளி (Friday), சனி (Saturday). Planet-named like most of Asia — செவ்வாய் (Mars), புதன் (Mercury), வியாழன் (Jupiter), வெள்ளி (Venus), சனி (Saturn) — the sky keeps Tamil's calendar.

Day-parts steer greetings and meals: காலை (morning — காலை வணக்கம்), மதியம் (afternoon — lunch/saappaadu o'clock), மாலை (evening — மாலை வணக்கம், filter kaapi round two), இரவு (night — இரவு வணக்கம்? rare; goodnight is usually just வணக்கம் with a smile).

Bigger units plan life: வாரம் (week), மாதம் (month), வருடம் (year) — அடுத்த வாரம் (next week), சென்ற மாதம் (last month), இந்த வருடம் (this year). Tamil plans in weeks for errands, months for visits, years for weddings.

Dates assemble simply: தேதி (thedhi — date), முதல் தேதி (first), இன்று என்ன தேதி? (what's today's date?). Numbers from the numbers page slot straight in — பதினைந்தாம் தேதி (the 15th). Time, dates, plans: one page, total coverage.
topics.title: Time and dates

topics.desc: Stations, directions, tickets and toilets — travel Tamil that gets you there. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ...எங்கே? (...enge — where is...?) plus a pointing finger. பேருந்து நிலையம் எங்கே? ரயில் நிலையம் எங்கே? One pattern, every destination in Tamil Nadu.
faqs.q: How do I ask where things are?

faqs.a: இடது (left), வலது (right), நேராக (straight) — then அருகில் (near) and தூரம் (far). Tamil directions come with generous hand-waving; watch the hands as well as the words.
faqs.q: Left, right, straight?

faqs.a: கழிவறை எங்கே? (where is the toilet?) — say it clearly, without embarrassment. Every bus stand, station and restaurant understands instantly.
faqs.q: How do I find a toilet?

topics.lede: Stations, directions, tickets and toilets — travel Tamil that gets you there.

links.desc: Journeys in course order, with drills.
links.label: Tamil travel

links.desc: Use these lines in real exchanges.
links.label: Tamil conversation lessons

topics.note: A note on நிலையம். நிலையம் (nilaiyam — station/stand) anchors every journey: பேருந்து நிலையம் (bus stand), ரயில் நிலையம் (railway station), விமான நிலையம் (airport). Learn the pattern once — vehicle + நிலையம் — and every signboard in Tamil Nadu reads itself.
paras: Destinations unlock with one ending: பேருந்து நிலையம் (bus stand), ரயில் நிலையம் (railway station), விமான நிலையம் (airport), ஹோட்டல் (hotel). Add எங்கே? (where?) and you can find every transport hub in the state — நிலையம் எங்கே? is the traveller's master key.

Directions come in threes: இடது (left), வலது (right), நேராக (straight ahead) — plus அருகில் (nearby) and தூரம் (far). இடது பக்கம் (on the left side), நேராகப் போங்கள் (go straight) — follow the words, watch the inevitable hand gestures, arrive smiling.

Tickets and seats run the journey: டிக்கெட் (ticket), ஒரு டிக்கெட் (one ticket), எவ்வளவு? (how much?), இருக்கை (irukkai — seat). பேருந்து எப்போது வரும்? (when does the bus come?) — asked at every stand, answered with cheerful vagueness. Patience is also vocabulary.

Emergencies and essentials close the kit: உதவி (help), கழிவறை எங்கே? (where is the toilet?), தண்ணீர் (water), மருத்துவமனை (hospital). Hope never to need உதவி செய்யுங்கள் (please help) — but carry it always, like travel insurance in a single word.
topics.title: Travel phrases

topics.desc: Prices, bargaining and colours — shop in Tamil from first price to final deal. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: விலை என்ன? (what's the price?) — then எவ்வளவு? (how much?) for everything else. Two questions, every shop in Tamil Nadu.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

faqs.a: மிகவும் விலை அதிகம் (too expensive) with a smile, then கொஞ்சம் குறையுங்கள் (reduce a little, please). Bargaining is friendly theatre — play your part warmly and the price moves.
faqs.q: How do I bargain politely?

faqs.a: Start with five: சிவப்பு (red), நீலம் (blue), பச்சை (green), மஞ்சள் (yellow), வெள்ளை (white). வேறு நிறம் (different colour) shows them all.
faqs.q: Which colours first?

topics.lede: Prices, bargaining and colours — shop in Tamil from first price to deal.

links.desc: Markets in course order, with drills.
links.label: Tamil shopping

links.desc: Use these lines in real exchanges.
links.label: Tamil conversation lessons

topics.note: A note on குறையுங்கள். கொஞ்சம் குறையுங்கள் (konjam kuraiyungal — please reduce a little) is the magic sentence of Tamil markets. Said smiling, it opens every negotiation; said with வாங்குகிறேன் (I'll buy it) right after, it closes most. Bargaining respects the dance — never the demand.
paras: Prices open every transaction: விலை என்ன? (what's the price?), எவ்வளவு? (how much?), இது என்ன விலை? (what's this one's price?). Listen for the number plus ரூபாய் — repeat it back to confirm — ஐம்பது? (fifty?) — and you are already shopping in Tamil.

Bargaining follows the friendly script: மிகவும் விலை அதிகம் (too expensive), கொஞ்சம் குறையுங்கள் (reduce a little), சலுகை உண்டா? (any discount?). Start walking away slowly — நன்றி, பார்க்கிறேன் (thanks, I'll look around) — and the real price often chases you down the street.

Sizes and colours refine the hunt: பெரியது (the bigger one), சிறியது (the smaller one), புதியது (a new one), வேறு நிறம் (a different colour). Point, name the change, nod — Tamil shopkeepers read gestures fluently and reward attempts instantly.

Colours close the sale: சிவப்பு (red), நீலம் (blue), பச்சை (green), மஞ்சள் (yellow), வெள்ளை (white), கருப்பு (black). சிவப்பு நன்றாக இருக்கிறது (the red looks good) — then வாங்குகிறேன் (I'll take it). Deal done, in Tamil, with a smile on both sides.
topics.title: Shopping and bargaining

topics.desc: Help, doctor, hospital — emergency Tamil you hope to never need. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: உதவி செய்யுங்கள் (please help) — loud, clear, repeated. Add எங்கே மருத்துவமனை? (where is the hospital?) and Tamil crowds mobilise instantly.
faqs.q: What is the one emergency sentence?

faqs.a: Point and say இங்கே வலிக்கிறது (it hurts here). Then உடம்பு சரியில்லை (I feel unwell) and மருத்துவர் வேண்டும் (I need a doctor). Pain plus pointing crosses every language gap.
faqs.q: How do I explain pain?

faqs.a: தொலைந்துவிட்டது (it is lost) — பணம் தொலைந்துவிட்டது (money lost), பை தொலைந்துவிட்டது (bag lost). Then போலீஸ் நிலையம் எங்கே? (where is the police station?).
faqs.q: How do I report something lost?

topics.lede: Help, doctor, hospital — emergency Tamil you hope to never need.
topics.note: A note on உதவி. உதவி (udhavi — help) is Tamil's shortest lifeline — shout it and crowds come running. Tamil Nadu's bystander culture is famously kind: strangers will escort you to hospitals, translate for doctors, and refuse thanks. Ask loudly; receive gratefully.
paras: The core three save lives: உதவி (help), ஆபத்து (danger), அவசரம் (emergency). உதவி செய்யுங்கள் (please help me) — say it to anyone, anywhere. Tamil crowds respond to distress calls faster than any app; your job is only to ask.

Medical words route the rescue: மருத்துவர் (doctor), மருத்துவமனை (hospital), மருந்து (medicine), மருந்தகம் (pharmacy). மருத்துவமனை எங்கே? (where is the hospital?) plus a taxi wave — in cities, help arrives in minutes.

Symptoms speak simply: இங்கே வலிக்கிறது (it hurts here — point!), உடம்பு சரியில்லை (I feel unwell), தலைவலி (headache), காய்ச்சல் (fever). Pain words plus pointing hands diagnose across every language barrier on earth.

Danger and loss close the kit: தீ (fire), திருடன் (thief), போலீஸ் (police), தொலைந்துவிட்டது (it's lost), தூதரகம் (embassy). Memorise these cold — emergencies never wait for phrasebooks, and ten minutes of drilling buys total peace of mind.
topics.title: Emergency Tamil

topics.desc: நீங்கள் or நீ? வாருங்கள் or வா? Respect levels, decoded with examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: நீங்கள் for every adult you don't know well — shopkeepers, officials, elders, strangers. நீ waits for close friends, children and family. Wrong-side errors embarrass; learners are forgiven, but respect first is always safest.
faqs.q: When do I use நீங்கள்?

faqs.a: Add -ங்கள்: வா becomes வாருங்கள், போ becomes போங்கள், சொல் becomes சொல்லுங்கள். One ending, instant politeness — the highest-value suffix in Tamil.
faqs.q: How do I make a command polite?

faqs.a: ஐயா (aiyaa — sir) and அம்மா (ammaa — madam) address strangers respectfully — ஐயா, நேரம் என்ன? (sir, what time is it?). Better than pointing and shouting in any language.
faqs.q: How do I address strangers?

topics.lede: நீங்கள் or நீ? வாருங்கள் or வா? Respect levels, decoded.
topics.note: A note on அவர்கள். அவர்கள் (avargal — they / he-or-she formal) does double duty: plural they AND singular respect — அவர் வருகிறார் (he/she formal comes) elevates one person with plural grammar. Tamil respect literally multiplies the person.
paras: Tamil has two yous: நீங்கள் (formal/plural — strangers, elders, officials) and நீ (familiar — friends, children, family). English erased this distinction centuries ago; Tamil keeps it razor-sharp. Every conversation opens with an invisible choice — make it consciously, and make it respectful.

Verbs mirror the split: வாருங்கள் (please come) versus வா (come!), சொல்லுங்கள் (please say) versus சொல் (say!), போங்கள் (please go) versus போ (go!). The -ங்கள் ending is pure respect — same verb, different universe. Stem-alone orders bark; -ங்கள் invites.

Giving and forgiving show the range: தாருங்கள் (please give) versus கொடு (give!), மன்னியுங்கள் (please forgive) versus மன்னித்துவிடு (forgive, familiar). Beggars and kings both hear தாருங்கள் — politeness in Tamil costs nothing and buys everything.

Strangers get titles: ஐயா (sir), அம்மா (madam/mother), அண்ணா (brother), அக்கா (sister). ஐயா, உதவி செய்யுங்கள் (sir, please help) opens any door; barking orders at strangers closes them. Tamil warmth is earned with two syllables of respect.
topics.title: Formal and informal Tamil

topics.desc: Verb-first sentences, நான் வேண்டும், இல்லை vs அல்ல — fix the classic errors. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: English order with Tamil words: நான் போ instead of நான் போகிறேன், verb first, question words misplaced. Cure: every sentence ends with the verb — practise SOV until English order feels foreign.
faqs.q: What is the most common mistake?

faqs.a: Wanting flows toward people: எனக்கு வேண்டும் (to-me it-is-wanted), never நான் வேண்டும். One of Tamil's deepest patterns — experiences come TO you — and beginners fight it for weeks.
faqs.q: Why is நான் வேண்டும் wrong?

faqs.a: இல்லை denies existence and possession — பணம் இல்லை (no money); அல்ல denies identity — நான் மாணவன் அல்ல (I am not a student). Two no's, two jobs, zero overlap.
faqs.q: இல்லை or அல்ல?

topics.lede: Verb-first sentences, நான் வேண்டும், இல்லை vs அல்ல — fix them all.
topics.note: A note on தவறு. தவறு (thavaru — mistake) is the kindest word in this lesson — என் தவறு (my mistake) disarms every situation. Tamils adore learners who err boldly and laugh warmly; the only true தவறு is silence.
paras: Mistake one: English word order. நான் போ (I go — bare stem, wrong) instead of நான் போகிறேன் (I go — conjugated, right); verbs wandering mid-sentence instead of anchoring the end. Tamil is verb-final, always — SOV is not a suggestion, it is the law.

Mistake two: நான் வேண்டும் (I want — wrong) instead of எனக்கு வேண்டும் (to-me wanted — right). Tamil wanting flows toward the wanter; English wanting fires from the wanter. Flip the arrow and dozens of sentences — எனக்குப் புரிகிறது, எனக்குத் தெரியும் — unlock at once.

Mistake three: one-size no. இல்லை denies existence — பணம் இல்லை (there's no money); அல்ல denies identity — நான் ஆசிரியர் அல்ல (I am not a teacher). Beginners spray இல்லை everywhere; natives smile and correct. Learn both no's, use each precisely.

Mistake four: rushing sounds — flat long vowels (கல் for கால்), merged n's, skipped -ங்கள். மெதுவாக (slowly), சரியாக (correctly), மீண்டும் (again): the holy trinity of repair. முயற்சி (effort) plus பயிற்சி (practice) plus பொறுமை (patience) — and வாழ்த்துக்கள், mistakes become fluency.
topics.title: Mistakes every learner makes

topics.desc: Stop translating in your head — shadowing, thinking aloud and brave first speeches. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Shadow natives: play a Tamil sentence, repeat it aloud half a second behind, matching rhythm and melody. Ten minutes daily rewires your mouth faster than any textbook.
faqs.q: What is the fastest speaking drill?

faqs.a: Yes — narrate your day in Tamil: நான் காபி குடிக்கிறேன் (I'm drinking coffee), நான் பள்ளிக்குப் போகிறேன். Thinking aloud turns dead time into speaking practice.
faqs.q: Should I talk to myself in Tamil?

faqs.a: Perfectionism. Tamils reward every attempt and correct with love — பேசுங்கள், தவறு பரவாயில்லை (speak, mistakes are fine). Fluency is corrected mistakes, stacked daily.
faqs.q: What blocks speaking most?

topics.lede: Stop translating in your head — shadowing, thinking aloud, brave speeches.

links.desc: Dialogues with audio, step by step.
links.label: Tamil conversation lessons

links.desc: Speak these lines until they are yours.
links.label: Tamil practice lab

topics.note: A note on பேசலாம். பேசலாம் (peesalaam — let's speak / we may speak) is permission and invitation in one word — வாருங்கள், தமிழில் பேசலாம் (come, let's speak in Tamil). Say it to every patient listener; doors, hearts and vocabularies open together.
paras: Speaking starts with shadowing: play a Tamil line, echo it half a beat behind, copying music more than words. உரையாடல் (conversation) is rhythm before grammar — shadow ten minutes daily and your mouth learns Tamil's dance while your brain watches.

Questions and answers volley practice: கேள்வி (question) out, பதில் (answer) back. Ask yourself everything — இது என்ன? எங்கே? ஏன்? — and answer aloud. Self-volleys feel silly for a day, then feel like fluency arriving.

Opinions and stories stretch speeches: கருத்து (opinion), உண்மை (truth), கதை (story). என் கருத்து... (in my opinion...) forces full sentences; கதை சொல்லுங்கள் (tell a story) forces sequences. Opinions build sentences; stories build speakers.

Courage closes the circuit: தைரியம் (courage) speaks first and perfects later. பாட்டு (songs) loosen tongues, சிரிப்பு (laughter) dissolves fear, அமைதி (pauses) are allowed. Speak badly today — பேச்சு (speech) improves only in motion.
topics.title: Speaking practice

topics.desc: Fast speech, films and radio — train your ears until Tamil sounds slow. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Spoken Tamil contracts: போகிறேன் melts toward போறேன், வருகிறேன் toward வரேன். Learn the full forms first, then meet the street forms — this page bridges both.
faqs.q: Why is spoken Tamil so fast?

faqs.a: Children's films and songs first — clear speech, simple stories, endless repetition. Then வானொலி (radio) dramas, then full திரைப்படம் (cinema). Difficulty ladders beat difficulty cliffs.
faqs.q: What should I listen to first?

faqs.a: Catch the question words — என்ன, எங்கே, யார், எப்போது — and the verb at the end. Questions plus verbs carry eighty percent of meaning; the rest is decoration.
faqs.q: How do I catch meaning in fast speech?

topics.lede: Fast speech, films and radio — train your ears until Tamil sounds slow.

links.desc: Sounds in course order, with drills.
links.label: Tamil pronunciation

links.desc: Dialogues with audio, step by step.
links.label: Tamil conversation lessons

topics.note: A note on புரிகிறதா? புரிகிறதா? (purigiradhaa — do you understand?) is the kindest question in Tamil — teachers, friends and auto drivers ask it constantly. Answer புரிகிறது (understood) or கொஞ்சம் கொஞ்சம் (little by little); honesty tunes every speaker to your level.
paras: Listening begins with attention: கவனம் (attention) — கவனமாகக் கேளுங்கள் (listen carefully). Tamil sentences save the verb for last, so ears must hold the whole sentence before meaning lands. Patience is a listening skill; practise holding, not guessing.

Street Tamil contracts beautifully: போகிறேன் → போறேன், வருகிறேன் → வரேன், இருக்கிறது → இருக்கு. Textbooks teach the full forms; ears must learn the melted ones. Listen for the verb-ghost at sentence end — the meaning hides there.

Media ladders the difficulty: பாடல் (songs) first — slow, repetitive, emotional; செய்தி (news) next — clear, formal, standard; வானொலி (radio) drama third — fast, natural, fun; திரைப்படம் (films) last — slang, speed, glory. Climb rung by rung; never leap.

Active listening closes the loop: மீண்டும் கேளுங்கள் (listen again), ஒலி (sound) by ஒலி. Replay each line three times — once for music, once for words, once for meaning. Three passes per line, ten lines per day: ears transform within a month.
topics.title: Understanding spoken Tamil

topics.desc: Words to sentences to stories — reading Tamil from first signs to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Signboards: கடை (shop), நிலையம் (station), உணவகம் (restaurant) — big letters, daily repetition, instant rewards. Streets teach faster than textbooks.
faqs.q: What should I read first?

faqs.a: Children's books — short வாக்கியம் (sentences), pictures for context, full pulli marks. Then comics, then செய்தித்தாள் headlines, then articles.
faqs.q: When am I ready for books?

faqs.a: Keep an அகராதி (dictionary) app open and mine unknown words — five per page, no more. Reading with a dictionary beats studying word lists: context glues memory.
faqs.q: How do I handle unknown words?

topics.lede: Words to sentences to stories — reading from first signs to full pages.
topics.note: A note on செய்தித்தாள். Tamil newspapers — தினத்தந்தி, தினமலர் — use formal written Tamil (செந்தமிழ்-flavoured), nobler than street speech. Headlines first: big type, short lines, daily habit. One headline a day keeps illiteracy away.
paras: Reading starts with words: வார்த்தை (word) by வார்த்தை — படியுங்கள் (please read) signs, labels, names. Tamil spelling mirrors speech, so sounding out works: see கடை, say kadai, know shop. Phonetic scripts reward beginners richly.

Sentences assemble next: வாக்கியம் (sentence) — subject, object, verb-last. Read SOV sentences end-first for meaning: find the verb, then ask who-did-what. Backwards parsing feels odd for a week, then automatic forever.

Paragraphs and articles follow: பத்தி (paragraph), கட்டுரை (article), கவிதை (poem). Children's stories first — short, illustrated, kind — then பத்திரிகை (magazines), then இலக்கியம் (literature) itself. Tamil's written heritage spans two thousand years; start at the shallow end.

Dictionaries deepen everything: அகராதி (dictionary) — five new words per page, written down, reviewed nightly. Reading without recording entertains; reading with recording teaches. Mine every page; keep every gem.
topics.title: Reading Tamil

topics.desc: Letters to lists to letters — writing Tamil from first strokes to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Curves before corners: Tamil letters flow round — அ, ஆ, உ, எ — so practise circles and hooks first. Trace big, shrink slowly; கையெழுத்து (handwriting) beautifies with mileage.
faqs.q: How do I start writing Tamil?

faqs.a: பட்டியல் (lists): shopping lists, word lists, daily plans. Lists forgive grammar, demand spelling, and get used — the perfect beginner writing.
faqs.q: What should I write first?

faqs.a: கடிதம் (letters) to friends, குறிப்பு (notes) to self, வீட்டுப்பாடம் (homework) for courses. Real writing to real readers beats copied exercises every time.
faqs.q: When real writing?

topics.lede: Letters to lists to letters — writing from first strokes to full pages.
topics.note: A note on கையொப்பம். Your கையொப்பம் (signature) in Tamil script is a milestone — practise it until it flows in one confident motion. Signing Tamil-style on forms, cards and letters declares belonging more than any certificate.
paras: Writing starts with strokes: Tamil letters curve and loop — எழுதுங்கள் (please write) circles, hooks and waves before full letters. Trace அ ஆ இ ஈ உ ஊ big and slow; the hand learns shapes the eye already knows.
Tools matter little, mileage matters all: எழுதுகோல் (pen), pencil, finger on steamed mirrors — Tamil children trace in rice, sand and air. Write everywhere; medium is vanity, motion is learning.

Lists graduate the hand: பட்டியல் (list) — குறிப்பு (notes), முகவரி (addresses), தேதி (dates). Copy your own பெயர் (name) fifty times, then friends' names, then street names. Familiar words, fresh script: the fastest fluent hand.

Real writing arrives: கடிதம் (letters), விண்ணப்பம் (applications), தேர்வு (exams), வீட்டுப்பாடம் (homework). Write a postcard to yourself in Tamil — short, joyful, posted. First posted Tamil is never forgotten.
topics.title: Writing Tamil

topics.desc: Who does what, verb last — Tamil sentences decoded with living examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Subject-Object-Verb: நான் புத்தகம் படிக்கிறேன் (I book read). Endings mark roles, so order flexes for emphasis — but verb-last is home.
faqs.q: What is Tamil word order?

faqs.a: Tense lives on the verb: போகிறேன் (go-present), போனேன் (went), போவேன் (will go). Time words — நேற்று, இன்று, நாளை — frame it; the verb carries it.
faqs.q: How do tenses work?

faqs.a: Add -ஆ and rise: அது உன் புத்தகமா? (is that your book?). Question words — என்ன, எங்கே, யார் — sit where the answer would.
faqs.q: How do I ask questions?

topics.lede: Who does what, verb last — sentences decoded with living examples.
topics.note: A note on மழை பெய்கிறது. Tamil weather does things: மழை பெய்கிறது (rain rains), வெயில் அடிக்கிறது (sun strikes), காற்று வீசுகிறது (wind blows). No empty it — Tamil skies act. Weather sentences teach SOV with zero confusion: subject, then verb, done.
paras: Simple sentences stack three blocks: நான் பள்ளிக்குப் போகிறேன் (I — to-school — go), அவள் பாட்டு பாடுகிறாள் (she — song — sings), நாங்கள் தமிழ் படிக்கிறோம் (we — Tamil — study). Subject, object, verb — build a hundred of these and Tamil skeleton is yours.

Animals make perfect practice: குழந்தை சிரிக்கிறது (the child laughs), நாய் குரைக்கிறது (the dog barks), பூனை தூங்குகிறது (the cat sleeps). Short subjects, vivid verbs, zero ambiguity — describe every creature you meet and SOV becomes reflex.

Time flexes the frame: நான் நாளை வருவேன் (I'll come tomorrow), நேற்று மழை பெய்தது (it rained yesterday). Time words float — front for emphasis, middle for flow — while the verb holds the end. Tense plus time word: past, present, future, mastered.

Identity and questions close the set: இது என் வீடு (this is my house), அது உன் புத்தகமா? (is that your book?), எல்லாம் சரி (all is well). Equate with இது/அது, question with -ஆ, reassure with எல்லாம் சரி — sentences for every situation.
topics.title: Tamil sentence structure

topics.desc: Rahul becomes ராகுல் — spell, write and own your name in Tamil script. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Sound it out in Tamil letters: Rahul → ராகுல், Priya → பிரியா, John → ஜான். Tamil spells by ear — say your name slowly, catch each sound, write each letter.
faqs.q: How do I write my name in Tamil?

faqs.a: Grantha letters — ஜ (ja), ஷ (sha), ஸ (sa), ஹ (ha), க்ஷ (ksha) — handle foreign sounds. ஜான் (John), ஷர்மிளா? — borrowed letters for borrowed names, fully Tamil now.
faqs.q: What about sounds Tamil lacks?

faqs.a: முதல் எழுத்து (first letter) starts it, கடைசி எழுத்து (last letter) ends it. Introduce with என் பெயர்... (my name is...), then write it — introductions stick twice as well written.
faqs.q: How do I introduce my name?

topics.lede: Rahul becomes ராகுல் — spell, write and own your name in Tamil.
topics.note: A note on ராகுல் vs ராஹுல். Foreign h floats in Tamil names — Rahul appears as ராகுல், ராஹுல், even ரகுல். All are read Rahul; none is wrong. Tamil welcomes foreign names with flexible spelling — pick the shape you love and own it.
paras: Names transliterate by ear: break yours into sounds, match each to Tamil letters — முருகன் (Murugan), லட்சுமி (Lakshmi), கண்ணன் (Kannan) show the pattern. Say it slow, write it true — எழுத்துக்கூட்டு (spelling) by sound, not by English letters.

Foreign sounds borrow Grantha letters: ஜ for John (ஜான்), ஷ for Sharma sounds, ஹ for hotels and Rahuls, ஸ for stars. These Sanskrit-born letters are Tamil citizens now — use them proudly for every imported sound.

Introductions pair speech and script: அறிமுகம் (introduction) — என் பெயர்... (my name is...), spoken, then written. பெயர் பலகை (name boards) on doors and desks teach daily — read every board, collect every name.

Nicknames warm everything: புனைபெயர் (nickname) — செல்லம் (darling), கண்ணா (dear), தங்கம் (gold). Tamil shortens with love: Murugan becomes முருகு, Lakshmi becomes லட்சு. Earn a Tamil nickname and you have arrived.
topics.title: Write your name in Tamil

topics.desc: செம, மச்சான், வேற லெவல் — street Tamil that films, friends and fun run on. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: செம (sema — awesome) and சூப்பர் (super) — positive, universal, safe. Sprinkle them on food, films and friends; instant insider status.
faqs.q: What slang is safe everywhere?

faqs.a: மச்சான் (dude/bro) and மச்சி (buddy) — for friends only, never elders or strangers. Friendship slang misused offends; rightly used, it bonds instantly.
faqs.q: Can I call people machchaan?

faqs.a: சும்மா (just like that / for fun) — சும்மா சொன்னேன் (just kidding), சும்மா வந்தேன் (just dropped by). The most Tamil word in existence: purposeless joy, declared proudly.
faqs.q: What does summaa mean?

topics.lede: செம, மச்சான், வேற லெவல் — street Tamil that fun runs on.
topics.note: A note on சும்மா. சும்மா (summaa) defies translation — just because, for fun, no reason, chill. ஏன்? — சும்மா (why? — just because). Whole philosophies hide in two syllables; use it freely, smile always.
paras: Praise slang opens doors: செம (awesome), சூப்பர் (super), வேற லெவல் (next level), அட்டகாசம் (fantastic), கலக்கிட்டே (you rocked it). Food, films, friends' outfits — praise everything loudly. Tamils praise generously; learners should too.

Friendship words bond crews: மச்சான் (dude), மச்சி (buddy) — friends-only, always warm. டேய் மச்சான் (hey dude) starts a thousand conversations daily. Never aim them upward at elders; sideways at friends, fire freely.

Reaction words colour stories: ஐயையோ (oh no!), அடடா (wow/oh!), கதை விடாதே (stop making things up!). Tamil storytelling runs on reactions — gasp, laugh, disbelieve theatrically. Flat faces kill stories; big reactions feed them.

Playful edges season everything: போடா (get lost — playful among friends, rude otherwise), காண்டு (frustration), சும்மா (just because). Learn the edges, respect the edges: slang's power is knowing exactly where fun ends.
topics.title: Tamil slang

topics.desc: Toys, moons, stars and good-child gold — Tamil for little learners, big joy. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Songs and கதை (stories) — பாட்டு with actions, tales with voices. Children absorb Tamil through music and play long before grammar.
faqs.q: How do kids learn Tamil best?

faqs.a: நல்ல பிள்ளை (good child) — praise every attempt loudly. Tamil parenting runs on encouragement; learners of all ages bloom under it.
faqs.q: How do I praise a child?

faqs.a: விளையாட்டு (games): name objects — பந்து! பொம்மை! — count steps, sing counts. Play first, words hitchhike.
faqs.q: Games or lessons?

topics.lede: Toys, moons, stars and gold stars — Tamil for little learners, big joy.
topics.note: A note on செல்லம். செல்லம் (sellam — darling/pet name) melts every Tamil heart — என் செல்லம் (my darling) for children, pets and beloveds. Terms of endearment are Tamil's mother tongue; every child swims in them.
paras: Little learners start with love: குழந்தை (child), பாப்பா (baby), செல்லம் (darling), நல்ல பிள்ளை (good child). Tamil childhood floats on affection-words — call every child செல்லம் and watch faces light like தீபாவளி.
Play teaches fastest: விளையாட்டு (play), பொம்மை (toy), பந்து (ball) — விளையாடலாம் (let's play)! Count throws, name colours, chase and giggle. Play first; Tamil hitchhikes on joy.

School words structure days: பள்ளிக்கூடம் (school), ஆசிரியர் (teacher), பாடம் (lesson), வீட்டுப்பாடம் (homework). வணக்கம் ஆசிரியர் (hello teacher) opens every school day — respect and learning, hand in hand.

Sky words spark wonder: சூரியன் (sun), நிலா (moon), நட்சத்திரம் (star) — நிலா காட்டு (show the moon)! Night-sky Tamil, whispered on terraces, becomes lifelong memory. Teach the sky; the child keeps the language.
topics.title: Tamil for kids
